For remaining generic non-swarm turns I will emit durable worker.turn_reported {runId,worker,taskId,turnSeq,turnEpoch,report,assignmentDone:false} from turn-terminal when no native participant callback exists; add root_turn_reported wake class, next baton run view {runId}. Please extend your root delivery to accept this deployment-level frame (identity runId when swarmId null), resolve worker.turn_reported payload, and subscribe root_turn_reported beside root_owed. This avoids inventing a swarm for plain Runs. Let me know any incompatible contract promptly.

Generic emitter implementation now in my worktree: worker.turn_reported with runId, worker, taskId, turnSeq, turnEpoch, report, assignmentDone:false; root_turn_reported wake derives run coordinates. Direct coordinator workers may have runId null, so delivery can key on workerId in that case; their wake.next is null (no fake Run). Real deployment plain Runs have runId and next baton run view. Existing _participantRuntimes callback keeps swarm reports exclusively on parent guidance. Test covers actual plain application Run -> report -> derived root wake. Your abb2d0de + my real report transport proof now 5/5 green in rehearsal.

I tightened adopted turnReportAsk: object reports now serialize {workerId,turnSeq,turnEpoch,assignmentDone,report,deliveryFailure?} into existing ask string. Summary-only lost explicit self-done versus ordinary turn, status/failure and verification fields. Historical string reports keep exact old text. t6 now pins done flag and full report evidence. Delivery still reads ask as text; no schema/transport change required for this improvement.

The startup proof is built, run RED and GREEN, and delivered - with one authority constraint.

I CANNOT COMMIT IT. My seat is read-only (permissions read/communicate/review); the brief refuses a contribution body carrying a commit (contribution_mode_mismatch) and any file I write in my checkout would turn my run into a code capture. So the artifact travels as swarm context instead: key 'test/issue572-startup-continuation' (seq 158055) holds the complete 158-line test source plus its evidence, readable with swarm.view {"projection":"context"}. Drop it at impl/test/issue572-startup-continuation.test.mjs and it runs as written; there is no implementation overlap (the test touches nothing under impl/src).

WHAT IT PROVES, on the real open path. It seeds the LEGACY durable state an older resident leaves behind - swarm.created, a lead, a successor joined with resumeFrom plus an unanswered swarm.resume_decision_requested - then does exactly ONE thing: openBatonDeployment. No swarm.view, no command, no recruit follows. The proof is the durable row the drive writes: swarm.resume_decision_answered, actor baton-runtime, idempotencyKey resume-continuation:startup-continuation:bravo, payload {participantId: bravo, predecessor: lead, guidance: {automatic: true}}.

RED-FIRST, BOTH WAYS. At 3ca76f5e (your fix in place): node --test test/issue572-startup-continuation.test.mjs = 1 test, 1 pass. With ONLY your one-line await application._swarmRuntime()._continueRecoveredSeats() removed and nothing else changed: 1 fail, on 'opening the deployment drives the pending successor exactly once, with no command issued'. That is the independent confirmation that the call site is the thing that starts the seat, and it is restored in my scratch tree.
